issues.failure_explanation: The Woodbury formula is (A+UCV)^{-1}=A^{-1}-A^{-1}U(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1}; the proof omits the inverse on the middle factor, yielding the false expressions (wi1),(wi2). For the scalar M=1 (r=n=1), (1+\lambda)^{-1} is not equal to 1/\lambda-(1+\lambda)/\lambda^3. The proof then compares two incorrect expansions that happen to coincide, so it does not establish the lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proof by the one-line argument M^T(MM^T+\lambda I_r)=(M^TM+\lambda I_n)M^T followed by multiplication by the two inverses, or apply Woodbury correctly.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's statement (the standard push-through identity) is true, but its given proof is invalid; results citing the lemma remain correct in substance.
issues.title: Woodbury identity misapplied in proof of push-through lemma (inverse of middle factor dropped)
issues.why_classification: The statement is a standard true identity with a trivial correct proof; no claim or dependent result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^T A_\tau)$ is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of $A_\tau^T A_\tau$.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix \tilde\lambda(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde\lambda I)^{-1} has eigenvalue 1 on the null space of A_\tau^TA_\tau, so its 2-norm is 1 whenever a block has fewer than n independent rows (the generic case, since blocks have floor(m/k) rows). The bound with the smallest *non-zero* eigenvalue only holds if x_t-x_\star lies in R(A_\tau^T), which is not established (membership in R(A^T) does not imply membership in R(A_\tau^T)). Counterexample: A=I_2, blocks {row 1},{row 2}, x_t-x_\star=e_2, \tau=1 gives x_{t+1}-x_\star=e_2 with no contraction, contradicting the claimed factor \tilde\lambda/(1+\tilde\lambda)<1. The 'equivalent' expectation bound and its rate \tilde\lambda/(\lambda_min^block+\tilde\lambda) inherit the failure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict to blocks with full column rank (floor(m/k) >= n, excluding the advertised sparse/underdetermined regimes) or replace the theorem by an expected-contraction analysis in terms of the spectrum of the averaged operator (e.g., \bar P), which is a different argument and rate.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's main convergence guarantee for Algorithm 1 (deterministic per-step and expected linear rate) is false in the regime the method targets (blocks with far fewer rows than n, e.g., all experiments with 100-row blocks); the advertised rate is meaningless.
issues.title: Per-block contraction bound in Theorem err_bound is false when A_tau^T A_tau is singular
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the stated per-step or expected linear rate survives; a valid result requires new proof architecture (averaging over the sampling) and changes the guarantee type and rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: But, these dynamic blocks can yield more ill-conditioned least-square problems.

issues.failure_explanation: The bounds in (errbound5) involve \lambda_{\min}^+(A_S^TA_S) and \lambda_{\max}(A_S^TA_S), which depend on the chosen row set S. Maximizing \|r_S\|^2 over S does not minimize \|r_S\|^2/\lambda_{\max}(A_S^TA_S) or \|r_S\|^2/\lambda_{\min}^+(A_S^TA_S): the largest-residual rows may be nearly collinear (as the paper itself notes), inflating \lambda_{\max} and deflating \lambda_{\min}^+, so another set S' can give strictly better bounds. The claim that both bounds are minimized is therefore unsupported, and a one-step reduction of bounds does not imply faster convergence over many iterations.

failure_location.quote: we minimize the above upper and lower bounds of the error $\|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|_2^2$ in \cref{eq:errbound5}, as $\lambda_{\min}^{+}, \lambda_{\min}^{-}$ are bounded for a given system, and thus ensure faster convergence in general over many iterations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement: using the uniform bound \lambda_{\max}(A_S^TA_S)\le\lambda_{\max}(A^TA), the maximal-residual block minimizes a block-independent upper bound on the one-step error; drop the lower-bound claim and the 'faster convergence in general' conclusion, or add an explicit assumption of uniformly comparable block spectra.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification for the residual-based dynamic block (and the introductory claim that it provably enhances SOBK's convergence) is not established.
issues.title: Convergence-boost argument ignores block-dependence of eigenvalue bounds
issues.why_classification: A contained, weaker but recognizably comparable statement (one-step upper bound optimization) is supportable; the stronger claims about both bounds and overall convergence must be dropped.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is the minimum residual-norm solution, since $x_k \in \mathcal{R}(A^T) \perp \mathcal{N}(A)$.
Therefore, when $x_k$ is an approximate solution of \eqref{eq:linear_system} obtained through \cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows x_k \in R(A^T). Membership in R(A^T) says nothing about the residual norm of an approximate iterate; it implies only that, if x_k is an exact solution of Ax=b, it is the minimum-norm solution. The stated conclusion that the (approximate) x_k minimizes \|b-Ax_k\|_2 is a non sequitur.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate: all iterates lie in R(A^T), so upon convergence to an exact solution the limit is the minimum 2-norm solution A^\dagger b.
issues.overall_effect: The remark's guarantee about the FAB-GMRES output is unsupported as stated.
issues.title: FAB-GMRES remark conflates membership in R(A^T) with minimizing the residual norm
issues.why_classification: The intended (min-norm at convergence) statement follows directly from the given argument; only the wording of the conclusion needs correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $r = b - A x_{j}$ and pick indices $\mathcal{I}$ of top $\left\lfloor \frac{m}{k} \right\rfloor$ squared elements $r_i^2$ where $i=1,2,\dots m$
Let us denote the sampling procedure of \cref{algo:roar-bk} as $\mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited convergence-in-mean result for regularized block Kaczmarz requires blocks drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution independent of the current iterate, so that E[x_{t+1}]-x^{(\mu)}=(I-\bar P)(E[x_t]-x^{(\mu)}). In Algorithm 1 the fourth block per iteration is chosen deterministically from the current residual r=b-Ax_j, so the 'sampling rule' depends on x_j; \bar W, \bar P and hence x^{(\mu)} in (eq:w_p) are not well-defined fixed objects, the expectation does not factor, and one ROR-BK iteration is a composition of four updates rather than a single sampled update. The theorem is therefore not a consequence of the cited result.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows from the Theorem 4.1 in \cite{ReRBK}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to the purely randomized part of the update (orthogonality-based sampling of fixed blocks, with \mu the fixed distribution \mathcal P and one update per step), for which the cited theorem applies; drop the claim for the residual-based dynamic block or supply a separate analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence of ROR-BK iterates in mean to a weighted least-squares solution (also advertised in the introduction) is unsupported for the algorithm as defined.
issues.title: Weighted least-squares convergence theorem cites a result whose iterate-independent sampling hypothesis ROR-BK violates
issues.why_classification: A comparable result survives for the randomized-block updates via the cited theorem, but the guarantee must be withdrawn for the residual-based step, which is a central feature of the method.
